newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES BEAT BLACKHAWKS FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES BEAT BLACKHAWKS FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Brian Holzinger's shorthanded goal with 2:44 left in the second period snapped a tie and Dominik Hasek made 43 saves as the Buffalo Sabres edged the Chicago Blackhawks 2-1 for their third straight win Monday.
Hasek stopped all 30 shots he faced over the final two periods for his 23rd victory of the season, tying him with Colorado's Patrick Roy and Philadelphia's Ron Hextall for the league lead.
"He's the best goalie in hockey right now, he keeps us in every game," Buffalo defenceman Garry Galley said.

In Boston, Kelly Miller had his first two-goal game in nearly three years and Joe Juneau broke a tie with a power-play marker in the second period as the Washington Capitals beat the Boston Bruins 3-2.
Miller tied the game at 1-1 at 8:48 of the first period when he backhanded the puck over Rob Tallas' left shoulder.
Jim Carey finished with 31 saves for the Capitals while Tallas made 23 stops for Boston, which fell to 9-13-5 on home ice.
Rob Ray also scored for Buffalo, and Sergei Krivokrasov scored for Chicago.
In Florida, Valeri Kamensky scored a pair of third-period goals to snap a tie, helping the Colorado Avalanche extend their unbeaten streak to 12 games with a 4-2 victory over the Florida Panthers.
Mike Ricci and Rene Corbet also scored for Colorado, which is 9-0-3 in its last 12 games.
Dave Lowry and Tom Fitzerald had goals for Florida.
In Hartford, Sean Burke made 44 saves and Kevin Dineen scored the decisive goal as the Hartford Whalers snapped a nine-game winless streak with a 3-1 victory over the reeling Toronto Maple Leafs.
Dineen, Keith Primeau and Andrew Cassels each had a goal and an assist for the Whalers.Sergei Berezin scored the lone goal for Toronto.
In Montreal, Mark Recchi followed up his hat trick in the All-Star game by scoring twice in a four-goal third period that lifted the Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory over the Detroit Red Wings.

Recchi, who was the Most Valuable Player of Saturday's All-Star Game in San Jose, scored the tying goal 21 seconds into the third period and added his 23rd of the season into an empty net with 39 seconds left.
Jocelyn Thibault made 35 saves for Montreal. Kris Draper scored for Detroit.

At the Islanders, former Islander Pierre Turgeon snapped a third-period tie with a wrap-around goal and added an empty-netter in the final seconds of the four-goal period to give the St. Louis Blues a 6-4 victory over the struggling New York Islanders.
Joe Murphy also scored twice for the Blues.
"It sort of a tough time, we're gonna try to salvage the situation," said Islanders coach Mike Milbury, who ran the team through a practice following the game.
"It's the worst game of the year on the effort level," Milbury said. "I'm responsible for discipline, motivation. That was not a motivated team."
In Vancouver, Markus Naslund scored twice as the Vancouver Canucks routed the San Jose Sharks 6-1 in a game that was postponed in December due to a blizzard in the Pacific Northwest.
Kirk McLean made 26 saves and Pavel Bure also scored on the power play for Vancouver.
